path_guard_nonblocking_finding.finding: The two consumer-manifest triggers are the thing that makes the parent's `npm ls next --workspace=... ` / `git diff --exit-code -- ... gui/app/package.json site/package.json` drift guard reachable for manifest-only PRs, yet nothing asserts they stay. The repo already commits workflow-inspection tests (this very file), so their absence here is an asymmetry: a later paths-filter edit would silently disable PR-time coverage for a manifest-only change with no red gate. The unfiltered `push: branches: [main]` leg still catches it post-merge, which is why this is not blocking. The explanatory comment above `paths:` also still enumerates only 'the js package, the npm workspace members + root lockfile/manifest, the wasm crates, this workflow file' and was not updated to name the consumer manifests it now watches.
path_guard_nonblocking_finding.suggestion: Add a one-line assertion to the committed workflow-inspection test that both manifests appear in `pull_request.paths`, and refresh the comment.

native_nonblocking.title: Lock key and hoisting assumed, not proven by a real install
native_nonblocking.detail: The script hardcodes packages['node_modules/sharp'] and resolves require('sharp') from the repo root. If npm ci nests the instance (e.g. node_modules/next/node_modules/sharp), require or the .version read throws. Failure mode is fail-closed (TypeError/MODULE_NOT_FOUND -> nonzero exit -> red step), so it cannot produce a false pass, but the error text would be opaque relative to the intended assertion message. Evidence (single recorded sharp lock instance, top-level-key advisory tooling) makes root hoisting the expected outcome; first real CI run confirms it.

native_nonblocking.title: Native/platform package identity not asserted
native_nonblocking.detail: Only sharp.versions.sharp (the JS wrapper package version) is compared to the lock. The selected @img/sharp-<platform> prebuilt version and sharp.versions.vips are printed but never asserted, so a drifted or substituted platform binary that still loads would pass. Printing full versions preserves diagnosability; consider asserting presence/shape of versions.vips later.

native_nonblocking.title: Weak byte-length bound
native_nonblocking.detail: assert.ok(data.length > 8) is satisfied by the signature check alone plus a few bytes; it is a liveness rather than a content check. Format/dimension/signature assertions carry the real weight.

native_nonblocking.title: Stub-only control coverage
native_nonblocking.detail: Positive/negative controls exercised control flow and exit-code propagation against a stub on Node 24.19.0. No real libvips/ABI execution and no Node 22 native compatibility claim; the packet states this limit explicitly.
